author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: La thoh ïa kane ka kot kat kum ki ktienrim bad 'tien tymmen katba lah ban kynmaw bad ban shem mynta na ki ktien jong phi.
english: This book has been written according to ancient words and traditional proverbs as much as can be remembered and found today from your own spoken language.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ban shu pyllait lymbiang ïa kane ka kot Niam tip-Blei tip-Briew donsot donkular ki Khasi, nga sngew sah pap halor lade.
english: To neglect publishing this book on the Khasi religion of knowing God and knowing humankind, righteousness and covenant, I feel sin remaining upon myself.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Mynta ki khun Khasi jong ngi kim don jingïahikai jingïapule shuh shaphang ka Hok ka sot ha la ïing la ïing kumba don ha kibarim.
english: Today our Khasi children no longer receive home instruction and learning regarding Truth and Righteousness as existed among the ancestors.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ha shnong ruh kim don tymmen shuh ki ban sneng ban kraw shnong kumba ju don mynno mynno.
english: In the villages too, there are no longer elders to counsel and guide the village community as was customary in bygone days.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka ïalum-ïalang ban ïathir ïa ka dei ka lait ruh ym ju sotan shuh.
english: Gatherings to deliberate together upon what is righteous and what is transgressive are no longer convened.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Khasi u ngeit ba u briew u wan sha kane ka pyrthei tang ban kamai ïa ka Hok.
english: The Khasi believes that man comes into this earthly world solely to earn Righteousness.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka Hok ka long ka nongrim jong ka jingim briew baroh kawei.
english: Righteousness is the bedrock foundation of all human life.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Lada u briew u duh ïa ka Hok, u duh ïa ka jingim bad ïa ka burom ha khmat U Blei.
english: If a person loses Righteousness, they lose life and honour before the face of God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ban kamai ïa ka Hok kam mut tang ka jingkylla spah, hynrei ka jinglong babha ha ka jingim.
english: To earn Righteousness does not mean acquiring material riches, but cultivating virtue and moral uprightness in life.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Uba im ha ka Hok, un ïoh ïa ka jingsuk bad ka jingshngaiñ ha ka shnong ka thaw.
english: He who lives in Righteousness shall obtain peace and security within the village community.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka Niam Khasi ka dei ka Niam Tip-Briew Tip-Blei.
english: The Khasi religion is the faith of Knowing Humankind and Knowing God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ym lah ban tip ïa U Blei lada ym da tip shwa ban burom bad sngewthuh ïa u briew.
english: One cannot know God unless one first learns to respect and understand fellow human beings.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Blei u Nongbuh Nongthaw u don ha ki bynta baroh jong ka mariang bad ka jingthaw.
english: God the Sovereign Creator is present across all realms of nature and creation.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Blei u ym don dur don dar, hynrei u don ka bor bad ka jingshai kaba khraw.
english: God possesses no physical form or idol, yet possesses infinite power and great divine light.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Khasi kim mane dur mane maw, hynrei ki mane ïa U Blei Uba U Nongthaw marwei.
english: The Khasis worship neither carved idols nor stones, but adore God the Supreme Creator alone.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jinglong Khasi ka shong ha ka Tip-Kur Tip-Kha.
english: Khasi identity and social order reside fundamentally in Knowing Maternal Kin and Paternal Relations.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Kur u dei u kpa-tymmen na ka liang ka kmie, bad u Kha u dei na ka liang u kpa.
english: The Kur constitutes the maternal clan from the mother's lineage, while Kha stems from the father's side.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Uba kheiñ-kur kheiñ-kha u long uba don akor bad uba don niam ha ka imlang sahlang.
english: He who honours matrilineal clan and paternal relations is recognized as courteous and pious in society.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka shongkha kur ka long ka sang kaba khraw tam kaba pynjot ïa ka jaidbynriew.
english: Endogamous marriage within the maternal clan is the gravest taboo and mortal sacrilege destroying the tribe.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka Mei-rad ka Kmie-tymmen ka long ka tynrai jong ka ïing ka sem bad ka kur ka jait.
english: The ancestral grandmother is the root foundation of the hearth, home, and matrilineal descent.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Blei u la buh ïa ka jutang bad u briew mynba u thaw ïa u ha pyrthei.
english: God established a divine covenant with man at the very dawn when He created him upon earth.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Kane ka jutang ka long ka ktien kaba u briew u la kular ban bat ha la ka rynieng.
english: This covenant represents the sacred pledge that humankind vowed to uphold throughout mortal existence.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba u briew u pynkheiñ ïa kane ka kular, ka sang bad ka ma ki wan ban tyllep ïa u.
english: Whenever man violates this covenant, severe ritual taboos and peril descend to engulf him.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka daw kaba pynjot ïa ka jinglong tymmen long san ka dei ka jinglait ktien bad jingshim kabu.
english: The underlying cause that ruins venerable traditions is breach of word and moral exploitation.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki tymmen ki ong ba ka ktien kaba la mih na ka shyntur kam lah shuh ban kylla dien.
english: The elders declare that the word once uttered from the mouth can never retreat backward.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Khasi ki kheiñ kyntang ïa ki khlaw kiba ki khot ki Law Kyntang bad Law Adong.
english: The Khasis regard as holy and sacred certain forest groves designated as Law Kyntang and Law Adong.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ym bit ban kheit syntiew, ban thoh dieng, lane ban pynjot ïa kawei ruh ka shynrain ha Law Kyntang.
english: It is forbidden to pluck flowers, fell trees, or harm a single dry twig within the Sacred Grove.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Ryngkew u Basa u sumar ïa ki khlaw bad ïa ki tyllong um jong ka shnong.
english: The guardian spirits Ryngkew and Basa protect the sacred forests and the village headwaters.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki ummat jong ka mariang ki kyrsoi na ki lum ban pyndap ïa ki wah duid bad ki wah bah.
english: The pristine waters of mother nature spring from the hills to replenish streams and mighty rivers.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jingpynjot mariang ka long ka jingbym khein burom ïa ka jingthaw U Blei.
english: The reckless destruction of nature constitutes gross disrespect toward the handiwork of God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba u Khasi u duwai, u kren ha ka ktien ba khuid khlem jingphikier ne jingshukor.
english: When a Khasi offers prayer, he speaks in pure language without hypocrisy or deceit.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka nguh ka dem ka long ka jingpynphai khmat sha U Blei Uba Lah Ban Leh Baroh.
english: Humble adoration and bowing represent turning one's face toward Almighty God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Syiem u dei u khlieh jong ka Hima, hynrei u dei tang u nongsumar ba la bynshet da ki paidbah.
english: The Syiem is the political head of the realm, yet serves merely as a custodian entrusted by the people.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Myntri bad ki Bakhraw ki ïa shong dorbar ban rai halor ki kam shnong kam hima.
english: The customary Ministers and Nobles sit in assembly council to deliberate on civic affairs of state.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Khasi ki ju pynieng mawbynna ban kynmaw ïa ki kpa-tymmen bad ki kmie-tymmen.
english: The Khasis traditionally erect upright megalithic stones (Mawbynna) in solemn remembrance of ancestral fathers and mothers.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U Maw-shynrang u ïeng pyrshah ïa ka sngi bad ka Maw-kynthei ka thiah pynkiang kum ka synduk.
english: The upright male stone stands facing the sun, while the flat female dolmen stone rests horizontally like a cist.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Kine ki maw kim dei ki blei, hynrei ki dei tang ki dak kynmaw ïa ka burom jong ka kur.
english: These monoliths are not deities worshipped, but enduring historical monuments commemorating the lineage honour of the maternal clan.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jingbuh mawbah ka pynïasoh lang ïa ki shyieng jong ka kur baroh hapoh kawei ka ling maw.
english: The final internment under the clan ossuary (Mawbah) unites the bones of all clan kin within a single stone sepulchre.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba la poi ka por ban buh mawbah, ka kur baroh ka wan khot ban ïa don bynta ha ka niam.
english: When the auspicious time arrives to inter remains in the clan ossuary, the entire clan is summoned to participate in the solemn rites.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Haba kha ïa u khunlung, ki ju pynlong ïa ka niam jer thoh ban ai kyrteng ïa u.
english: Upon the birth of an infant child, the naming ritual (Ka Jer Ka Thoh) is performed to bestow an auspicious name.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Lada u dei u shynrang ki buh ïa ka ryntieh bad ki khnam, lada ka dei ka kynthei ki buh ïa ka khoh bad u star.
english: If the babe be a boy they place a bow and arrows, while if a girl they place the conical basket (khoh) and woven headstrap (star).

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Ka ryntieh bad ki khnam ki thew ba un long u rangbah u ban ïada ïa ka kur bad ka hima.
english: The bow and arrows symbolize that he shall grow into a valiant warrior defender shielding clan and kingdom.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Ka khoh bad u star ki thew ba kan long ka nongri-ïing bad ka nongkamai spah jong ka ïing.
english: The conical basket and headstrap symbolize that she shall be the industrious keeper of hearth and domestic steward.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ha ka shongkurim, u kñi jong ka kynthei bad u kñi jong u shynrang ki ïakren ban pynskhem ïa ka jutang.
english: In solemn marriage matrimony, the maternal uncle of the bride and that of the groom negotiate to establish the sacred covenant.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jingïapynskhem ka long da kaba theh kiad bad duwai ha khmat U Blei bad ki sakhi.
english: The marriage pledge is solemnized by ceremonial libation and prayers offered before Almighty God and human witnesses.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: U tnga u wan shong ha ïing ka tnga kumba long ka dustur matrilocal jong ka jaidbynriew.
english: The husband takes up residence in the home of the bride in keeping with the ancient matrilocal matrilineal custom of the people.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Haba u briew u ïap, ki ong ba u la leit bam kwai ha ïing U Blei.
english: When a virtuous person passes away, the Khasis say that they have gone to partake of betel nut in the celestial House of God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka mynsiem kam ju ïap, hynrei ka leit phai biang sha U Nongthaw Uba la ai ïa ka.
english: The immortal human spirit never perishes, but returns home to the Supreme Creator who bestowed breath upon it.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Uba im ha ka pap bad ka sang un sa shah pynshitom bad un ym ïoh rung ha ka burom U Blei.
english: He who lived immersed in mortal sin and taboo shall endure spiritual affliction and be barred from entering divine glory.
